steps.title: Phase 4d judgment set (stone arch and ford)
steps.intro: Produced by tools/render_jobs/jobs/phase4d_judgment_set.json at 1920x1080. For every palette biome, a new 150 ft map (seed 1234) built with the real tools at human speed: a straight waist river along Z at x = -7, a straight ankle stream at x = 8, and a deep pond west of the river (brush 3.2 m along x = -17.5..-14 at z = 5; the water reaches about 3 m past the stroke, so the pond stays clear of the river's bank and of the arch's line). Through the crossing API (probes/crossing.gd place): a 2 m stone arch across the river at z = 2, a 2.5 m ford across it at z = -5, a 2 m ford across the ankle stream at z = 2, a 1.5 m plank bridge across the river at z = 8 for scale, and a 2.4 m arch along the pond's axis, long enough for a mid-stream pier and two barrels. Saved as a _p4d_ test level, then captured in authoring at home (grid on) and at zoom 8 on the river arch, the waist ford, the ankle ford and the pond arch; then played with tokens on the arch's deck, in both fords and on the plank deck, grid on, at home and at zoom 8 on the arch and the ford. Judge against the bar: painterly, a few bold soft-edged shapes rather than fine noise, a crossing that belongs to its biome (its own rock and paving, moss where it is damp), reads at tabletop zoom (8 to 14), never a slab or a stripe; ready when a newcomer dragging one line would keep it. Known faults to look for: the coping moss as a continuous green stripe along the parapet, the ford's landings as hard-edged rectangles, the submerged bar as uniform pale foam with no gravel, small marker stones on the ankle stream, a single-colour pier head, a flat grey arch; and per biome the sandstone paving and gravel on red sand, basalt in the cold biomes, moss amounts by climate, the wetland's reeds around a ford. The _p4d_ levels are kept for --saved look runs; jobs/cleanup_levels.json removes them.
